blocks.content: Igneous rocks are called primary rocks because they form the basis for the formation of all other rock types in the geological rock cycle.

rows: Cooling and crystallization of magma or lava
Crystalline texture, non-stratified, devoid of fossils
Deposition, compaction, and lithification of sediments
Thermal and dynamic alteration under extreme heat/pressure
Foliated or banded texture, highly dense and crystalline

items: Granite (Intrusive) and Basalt (Extrusive) are classic igneous rocks; Basalt dominates oceanic crust while Granite forms continental crust.
Standard metamorphism pairs frequently tested in matching questions: Limestone turns to Marble, Sandstone to Quartzite, and Shale to Slate.
Sedimentary rocks are distinct for their stratification (layering) and are the chief source of fossil fuels like petroleum, coal, and natural gas.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Igneous rocks form from the cooling and solidification of magma or lava and are categorized as primary rocks.
Sedimentary rocks are formed by the lithification and compaction of weathered sediments or organic remains over long periods.
Metamorphic rocks result from the recrystallization and structural change of pre-existing rocks under high heat and extreme pressure.
Fossils are found almost exclusively in sedimentary rocks, as extreme thermal and pressure conditions in igneous and metamorphic processes destroy organic material.
